reasons.content_decision_picture: Vanilla decision pictures and category art; ZIN decisions use their own sprites.
reasons.content_designer: Equipment designer art; the warfare spec gives the designers no equipment.
reasons.content_doctrine_icon: Vanilla doctrine icons; the warfare spec supplies ZIN doctrine icons.

reasons.content_idea_picture: Vanilla idea pictures; ZIN ideas use GFX_idea_zin_* sprites.
reasons.content_landmark: Vanilla landmark and famous-building pictures of the real world.
reasons.content_medal: Vanilla medals and ribbons; ZIN uses the Honours of the Field (spec 06).
reasons.content_operation: Vanilla operation pictures; the diplomacy spec keeps only the generic operation keys.
reasons.content_organisation: Vanilla organisation, policy and trait icons; the economy spec supplies the Erdae workshops.
reasons.content_portrait: Vanilla leader portraits; ZIN portraits are its own sprites.
reasons.content_technology_picture: Vanilla technology and equipment pictures; the warfare spec supplies ZIN pictures.
reasons.content_terrain: Scenery strips for the engine terrain types; their pictures belong to a content spec (an open item in the integration note).
reasons.content_texticon: A text icon outside the generic set; the reachability check proves no ZIN text names it.
reasons.content_trait: Vanilla trait icons; the warfare spec supplies ZIN trait icons.
reasons.content_unit_icon: Vanilla unit and ship counters; the warfare spec supplies ZIN unit icons.
reasons.country_mechanic: Art of a vanilla country mechanic; ZIN has no vanilla country tags.
reasons.country_scripted_gui: A vanilla country scripted GUI; it never loads because ZIN has no vanilla country tags.
reasons.debug_console: Developer console and error log art; not a player surface.
reasons.dlc_background: A DLC background thumbnail; replace_path removes the backgrounds it belongs to.
reasons.engine_drawn: The engine draws this element without a texture.
reasons.engine_fallback: The engine fallback texture for a missing sprite; it must stay a plain engine file.
reasons.engine_utility: A utility texture the engine blends with (transparency fade, dim overlay).
reasons.hidden_achievements: ZIN has no achievements; the screen and its art are hidden.
reasons.hidden_career: The career profile is a record across campaigns; its windows are hidden and inert (spec 06).
reasons.hidden_dlc: DLC banners, store and subscription widgets are hidden by the main menu override.
reasons.hidden_social_links: Community and marketing links are hidden; the homepage and privacy links stay.
reasons.keyboard_glyphs: Keyboard key glyphs shown in shortcut tooltips; neutral and engine-bound.
reasons.link_published: A link to a Paradox service or the privacy page; stays as published.
reasons.map_shader_mask: A map shader mask or pattern for army group lines; the engine reads its alpha as data.
reasons.missing_texture: The installed game has no file for this sprite, so there is nothing to replace; any reference is a vanilla defect already in the baseline.
reasons.online_assets: Paradox online service art outside the game folders.
reasons.operative_event: Operative event art; ZIN gives no operative events (spec 02 section 4.5).
reasons.orphan: No sprite and no window names this texture.
reasons.publisher_mark: Publisher and engine logos (Paradox, Clausewitz) stay as published.
reasons.special_project: Special projects: ZIN has one interim great work and no project window.
reasons.transparent_placeholder: A fully transparent engine placeholder; nothing to replace.
reasons.unreachable_window: Referenced only from windows ZIN cannot show.
reasons.war_escalation: War escalation art belongs to a vanilla scripted GUI.

decisions: Z rows describe ZIN-owned sprites (GFX_zin_*), which are not inventory rows; no vanilla sprite is classified Z. Vanilla content slots whose art a content spec owns are U, with the owning spec in the reason.
D (derived override) is reserved and unused, as the spec says.
A file with several frames is one row; its frame order and count come from the inventory only. A row with more than one frame uses fit strip, one cell per frame.

Alpha policy per R row: opaque when the vanilla texture is opaque, or shaped with 97% or more solid pixels; uniform:<a> for a uniform vanilla alpha; shape (the vanilla outline as a binary mask) for other keyed or shaped panels and frames; cell (the cell's own outline) for emblems and sockets.
exact falls back to cover when the cell and target aspect differ by more than 15%, as the spec says.

MIO (Erdae workshops), raids (night raids) and the international market (Great Fairs) are kept by the economy, warfare and institutions specs, so their windows are reachable and skinned; their per-organisation, per-policy and per-raid icons are U content. This overrides the "unreachable" rows of spec 02 section 4.9.
Special projects (one interim great work), equipment designers, carriers, vanilla country scripted GUIs and country-mechanic art are unreachable (U).
Balance-of-power art is reachable (the foundation spec keeps common/bop for the Golden Court); country-specific BoP art is U.

Sprites in an overridden .gfx (frontendmainviewbg, frontendmainviewbg_basic, small_background and the DLC small_background files) are O; the DLC small_background rows are U because replace_path removes their pictures.
Selected variants of icon strips (army_selected_icons and the like) share the cells of their normal strips.
Initiator and receiver variants of a relation icon share the cell of the relation kind; flipping and rotating are allowed operations, so scroll arrows come from one cell.
Icons with no spec-named emblem use the neutral sockets of ui-sockets until their own emblem sheet exists; this is chrome-complete, not emblem-complete.
The 18 small map-mode emblems and 70 alert emblems follow the frame order of the vanilla strip; the alert meanings come from alert_frames.json, read by an agent from the alert tooltip keys.
Army badges need 81 cells: three sheets (6x6, 6x6, 3x3), because a 9x9 sheet is beyond what the generator holds.
Texticons: the generic set (about 70 glyphs used by tooltips) is R; the rest are U until the localisation scan proves one reachable (check 4).
Vanilla files that no sprite names (backups, bak folders, unreferenced art in gfx/interface) are U orphans; if a script names one the reachability check fails the build.
The cursor, minimap and move-arrow files are R with their own writers (ui_cursors, ui_minimap); ui_reskin skips them and reports them as delegated.
Luminance is classed dark below 96, mid below 160 and light from 160 (mean luma, alpha weighted); each R row picks a cell of its sprite's class where the sheet has one.
